bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is a 4118-byte net-snmp config file with no CR or LF. Bytes 0..10 are ASCII `includefile`, byte 11 is form-feed `0x0c`, and bytes 12..4117 remain on the same line as the filename operand. In `snmplib/read_config.c`, the line-reading loop accumulates the whole file into `line`, `copy_nword()` parses `token = "includefile"` and leaves `cptr` pointing at the 4106-byte remainder, and the `includefile` handler is selected. The only present operand check rejects a blank remainder; vulnerable source does not perform the later fix's `strlen(cptr) + 1 >= SNMP_MAXPATH` test before path assembly. Because the first operand byte is `0x49` rather than `'/'`, `read_config()` takes the relative-path branch, initializes stack buffer `fname[SNMP_MAXPATH]` from the current config filename's directory prefix, and then executes `strlcat(fname, cptr, SNMP_MAXPATH)`. Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4095` in `__wrap_strlcat`, called from `read_config.c:951`, and ASan identifies the destination as the 4096-byte stack object `fname243`. The fixed commit adds the missing overlength rejection immediately before the vulnerable path-building branch.

source.code: if (fgets(line + linelen, linesize - linelen, ifile) == NULL) {
source.description: Source. The config reader copies attacker-controlled file bytes into the expandable `line` buffer. Because the staged witness has no CR or LF, repeated loop iterations accumulate the entire 4118-byte file into one config line that is later tokenized into `includefile` plus a 4106-byte operand.
source.value_from: The harness writes the staged `poc` bytes to `/tmp/libfuzzer-%d.config` and calls `read_config(filename, read_config_get_handlers("snmp"), 0)` (`testing/fuzzing/snmp_config_fuzzer.c:60-72`). The exact staged file is 4118 bytes with SHA-256 `5b56288ecb7560761101652cf373b8fc4ab69b151ef50433a05bd181eea2d6df`, has no `0x0a` or `0x0d`, and starts with bytes `69 6e 63 6c 75 64 65 66 69 6c 65 0c` (`includefile` plus form-feed).
source.note: This is the first project statement that materializes the witness into vulnerability-relevant parser state inside `read_config`; the fuzzer entry itself is an unscored harness boundary.

root_cause.description: Root cause. In the `includefile` handler, the only operand validation is a blank-line check. When the staged operand is present but 4106 bytes long, vulnerable code still proceeds directly to path construction without rejecting names whose length already reaches `SNMP_MAXPATH - 1`.
root_cause.note: Fixed commit `3bd6f29d9ecc28d17dca371606992a9a87fa7f13` inserts `if (strlen(cptr) + 1 >= SNMP_MAXPATH) { ... continue; }` immediately after this block. That missing check is the source-level obligation absent on the crashing path.

sink.description: ASan sink. The relative `includefile` path concatenates the attacker-controlled remainder string into stack buffer `fname[SNMP_MAXPATH]`, and the saved run crashes here with a stack-buffer-overflow write.
sink.note: Stage 01 reproduces `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4095` in `__wrap_strlcat`, called from this line. The frame report identifies stack object `fname243` at `read_config.c:935` occupying `[5408,9504)` and the invalid write starting at offset 9504, i.e. immediately past the 4096-byte buffer.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant tainted value is the `includefile` operand left in `cptr` after the first token is parsed.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Because byte 11 of the witness is `0x0c`, `copy_nword()` reads `token = "includefile"` and then `skip_white_const()` advances to byte 12. `cptr` therefore points at the remaining 4106 bytes of the same line, which `read_config` later treats as the filename argument.
tainted_value_origin.note: The `includefile` path uses the full remainder of the line rather than a second tokenized word, so `cptr` retains all 4106 trailing bytes.

parser_admitted.description: After tokenization yields `token == "includefile"`, the config parser dispatches into the `includefile` handler. Since the staged operand begins with `0x49` (`'I'`) rather than `'/'`, the later relative-path sub-branch reaches the crashing `strlcat()` site.

coarse_trace.summary: The line-reading loop accumulates the newline-free witness into one config line, and token parsing yields `token = includefile` plus a 4106-byte remainder string in `cptr`.

The `includefile` handler is selected; the only present guard rejects blank operands, but the missing length check leaves the overlong remainder live and `cptr[0] != '/'` selects relative-path assembly.

The relative branch derives the current directory prefix in `fname[SNMP_MAXPATH]` and then `strlcat`s the 4106-byte remainder into that stack buffer, matching the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow write.

fine_trace.note: Source. The line-reading loop appends attacker-controlled file bytes into heap buffer `line`. Because the staged witness contains no CR or LF, the loop keeps growing `line` and reading until EOF, so one logical config line is materialized with `linelen == 4118` before tokenization begins.

The line starts with non-whitespace `i`, so `skip_white(line)` returns the start of the buffer. `copy_nword()` then consumes the first word `includefile` and treats byte 11 `0x0c` as whitespace, leaving `token == "includefile"` and `cptr` pointing at byte 12, i.e. the remaining 4106 bytes of the same line.

The parsed keyword matches `includefile`, so control enters the includefile-specific handler instead of ordinary token processing. This is the only directive path that reaches the later filename-construction block.

The only present validation on the includefile operand is this blank-line check. For the staged witness `cptr` is non-NULL and still names 4106 remaining bytes, so execution continues. Vulnerable source has no `strlen(cptr) + 1 >= SNMP_MAXPATH` rejection here; the fix inserts that exact guard immediately after this block.

The first operand byte is `0x49` (`'I'`), not `'/'`, so this condition is false and `read_config()` takes the relative-path sub-branch. Only that sub-branch reaches `strlcat(fname, cptr, SNMP_MAXPATH)`.

In the relative branch, stack buffer `fname[SNMP_MAXPATH]` is initialized from the current config filename and then truncated at the last slash. On the staged path the caller filename comes from the fuzzer's `/tmp/libfuzzer-%d.config`, so `fname` becomes the directory prefix `/tmp/`. `SNMP_MAXPATH` resolves to `PATH_MAX`; the ASan frame layout confirms this `fname` object is 4096 bytes.

The unbounded 4106-byte remainder in `cptr` is concatenated into the 4096-byte stack `fname` built in step 6. The saved Stage 01 run crashes at this call with `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4095` in `__wrap_strlcat`; ASan identifies the destination as stack object `fname243` (`[5408,9504)`) in this frame.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_64315 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/snmp_config_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4095` in `__wrap_strlcat` from `read_config.c:951`.

format.name: single-line net-snmp config with overlong relative includefile operand
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 4118-byte file staged at `gt_results/arvo_64315/poc` (SHA-256 `5b56288ecb7560761101652cf373b8fc4ab69b151ef50433a05bd181eea2d6df`). Bytes 0..10 are ASCII `includefile`, byte 11 is form-feed `0x0c`, and bytes 12..4117 are the remainder of the same line. The file contains no `0x0a` or `0x0d`, so `read_config()` accumulates the whole witness into one config line and `copy_nword()` leaves `cptr` pointing to a 4106-byte operand whose first byte is `0x49`, not `'/'`. `includefile` uses that full remainder of the line as the filename argument, so this exact layout takes the relative-path branch and reproduces the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow write at `read_config.c:951`.
